185: | **Magenta** | Gross motor — can coordinate large movements | Rhythm tapping (simple beat: tap-tap-tap) | rhythm accuracy, consistency |
186: | **Red** | Power-body — explosive force, speed | Fast RT + rapid alternation (tap left-right-left-right fast) | speed, alternation accuracy |
187: | **Amber** | Disciplined body — sustained posture, endurance | Sustained hold + rhythm maintenance over time | endurance, consistency over time |
188: | **Orange** | Skilled body — multi-limb coordination, precision | Complex rhythm (polyrhythm: 3 against 2); precision tapping | polyrhythm accuracy, precision |
189: | **Green** | Expressive body — body as communication, flow | Free-form rhythm creation; "make a pattern that feels like X" | creativity, expressiveness (LLM for description) |
190: | **Turquoise** | Integrated body — body-mind unity, proprioceptive wisdom | Anticipatory timing (predict when stimulus will appear); body-scan accuracy | anticipation accuracy, interoceptive precision |
191: | **White** | Effortless body — wu-wei, action without actor | RT under no-urgency conditions; "respond when it feels right" | naturalness, consistency without effort |
192: 
193: ### 3.7 Willpower Line
194: 
195: | Stage | Qualitative structure | Assessment tasks | Key measures |
196: |---|---|---|---|
197: | **Infrared** | No volitional control — pure reflex | Cannot be assessed | — |
198: | **Magenta** | Impulse delay (seconds) — "wait for it" | Delay of gratification: wait 3s for bigger reward vs. tap now for small | choice, wait time |
199: | **Red** | Burst goals — intense short-term effort | Hold button for 3-5s under distraction; resist early-release temptation | hold duration, resistance to perturbation |
200: | **Amber** | Sustained effort — follow through on commitments | Hold for 8-12s; multi-trial consistency (don't degrade over trials) | duration, consistency across trials, no degradation |
201: | **Orange** | Strategic willpower — allocate effort wisely | Choose WHEN to exert effort (some trials are worth more); resource management | strategic allocation, total score optimisation |
202: | **Green** | Flexible willpower — hold AND release appropriately | Hold when told to hold, release when told to release (switching); "let go" tasks | switching accuracy, release speed, flexibility |
203: | **Turquoise** | Effortful effortlessness — sustained without strain | Long hold (15-20s) with minimal physiological cost (measured by consistency, not just duration) | consistency of hold (no jitter), smoothness |
204: | **White** | Wu-wei — action without actor, will without willing | "Hold until it feels right to release" (no external cue); self-determined timing | coherence of self-timing, non-reactivity to perturbation |
205: 
206: ### 3.8 Interpersonal Line
207: 
208: | Stage | Qualitative structure | Assessment tasks | Key measures |
209: |---|---|---|---|
210: | **Infrared** | No other — solipsistic | Cannot be assessed | — |
211: | **Magenta** | Other as extension of self — "you do what I want" | Simple imitation (NPC does X, you copy) | imitation accuracy |
212: | **Red** | Other as tool — transactional coordination | Predict NPC's simple pattern (repeating); "what will they do?" | prediction accuracy |
213: | **Amber** | Other as role — "what should they do?" (norm-based) | Predict NPC's behaviour based on their stated role/rules | role-based prediction, norm awareness |
214: | **Orange** | Other as mind — theory of mind, false belief | False-belief tasks: "NPC doesn't know X — what will they do?" | ToM accuracy, perspective-taking |
215: | **Green** | Other as subject — empathic coordination, mutual | Cooperative timing: sync with NPC who is also trying to sync with you | mutual adaptation speed, coordination quality |
216: | **Turquoise** | Other as self — non-dual relating, field awareness | Predict NPC's behaviour when NPC is adapting to YOU (recursive ToM) | recursive prediction accuracy, adaptation speed |
217: | **White** | No other — unity, spontaneous coordination | "Act together without communication" — emergent synchrony | synchrony quality, spontaneity |
218: 
219: ---
220: 
221: ## Part IV — Multi-Parameter Scoring
222: 
223: ### 4.1 Every assessment measures multiple dimensions
224: 
225: No assessment module produces a single number. Each produces a `Record<MeasureDimension, number>`:
226: 
227: | Dimension | What it measures | How |
228: |---|---|---|
229: | `accuracy` | Did they get it right? | % correct |
230: | `response_time` | How fast? (where speed matters) | Median RT, normalised |
231: | `consistency` | Same performance across trials? | Variance of accuracy/RT across trials |
232: | `depth` | How complex/nuanced was their response? | LLM scoring against rubric |
233: | `self_correction` | Did they catch and fix errors? | % of errors followed by correction |
234: | `complexity_handled` | What level of complexity could they manage? | Max difficulty level passed |
235: | `transfer` | Can they apply it in a new context? | Performance on novel variants |
236: | `metacognition` | Do they know what they know/don't know? | Prediction accuracy (predict own score) |
237: | `coherence` | Is their response internally consistent? | Cross-trial consistency of reasoning |
238: | `integration` | Can they hold multiple perspectives/dimensions? | Multi-factor response quality (LLM) |
239: 
240: ### 4.2 Dimension weights vary by line and stage
241: 
242: - **Cognitive:** accuracy (0.3), response_time (0.2), complexity_handled (0.3), self_correction (0.2)
243: - **Emotional:** accuracy (0.2), depth (0.3), consistency (0.2), integration (0.3)
244: - **Moral:** depth (0.4), coherence (0.3), integration (0.3) — accuracy is meaningless (no "right answer")
245: - **Intrapersonal:** depth (0.3), metacognition (0.3), coherence (0.2), self_correction (0.2)
246: - **Spiritual:** coherence (0.4), depth (0.3), consistency (0.3) — under temptation
247: - **Somatic:** accuracy (0.3), response_time (0.3), consistency (0.4)
248: - **Willpower:** consistency (0.3), complexity_handled (0.3), transfer (0.2), response_time (0.2)
249: - **Interpersonal:** accuracy (0.3), response_time (0.2), transfer (0.2), depth (0.3)
250: 
251: ### 4.3 LLM scoring for depth/coherence/integration
252: 
253: For lines where the response is qualitative (Moral, Intrapersonal, Spiritual, and higher stages of all lines), the LLM evaluates against a rubric:
254: 
255: ```ts
256: interface LLMScoringRequest {
257:   readonly playerResponse: string;
258:   readonly rubric: string;
259:   readonly stage: Stage;
260:   readonly line: Line;
261:   readonly dimensions: MeasureDimension[];
262: }
263: ```
264: 
265: The rubric is specific to the stage and line. Example for Moral/Green:
266: 
267: > "Score this response on a 0-1 scale for each dimension:
268: > - depth: Does the response acknowledge multiple valid perspectives without collapsing into relativism?
269: > - coherence: Is the reasoning internally consistent?
270: > - integration: Does it hold tension between competing goods without premature resolution?
271: > A Green-stage moral response recognises that all perspectives have partial truth, while still being able to act. It does not say 'anything goes' (that's regression to Red), nor does it impose a single principle (that's Orange)."
272: 
273: ---
274: 
275: ## Part V — The Assessment Engine
276: 
277: ### 5.1 How a stage assessment runs
278: 
279: ```
280: 1. Load the StageAssessment module for (line, stage)
281: 2. For each task in the module:
282:    a. Present the task to the player
283:    b. Collect their response (tap, choice, text, timing)
284:    c. Score the response on all relevant dimensions
285:    d. If LLM scoring needed: call evaluateResponse() with the rubric
286: 3. Aggregate dimension scores across all tasks
287: 4. Apply dimension weights from the scoring rubric
288: 5. Compare weighted score to passThreshold
289: 6. Return AssessmentResult { passed, confidence, dimensions }
290: ```
291: 
292: ### 5.2 Confidence calculation
293: 
294: Confidence is based on:
295: - **Number of trials:** more trials = higher confidence
296: - **Consistency:** low variance across trials = higher confidence
297: - **Discrimination:** clear pass or clear fail = higher confidence; borderline = lower
298: 
299: ```ts
300: function computeConfidence(results: TrialResult[], passThreshold: number): number {
301:   const score = weightedScore(results);
302:   const distance = Math.abs(score - passThreshold);
303:   const consistency = 1 - variance(results.map(r => r.score));
304:   const trialFactor = Math.min(1, results.length / 6);
305:   return distance * consistency * trialFactor;
306: }
307: ```
308: 
309: ### 5.3 Adaptive termination
310: 
311: Each module has a `minimumTrials` (usually 3-4) but can terminate early if:
312: - Confidence > 0.8 (clear pass or fail)
313: - All dimensions are clearly above or below threshold
314: 
315: This keeps the assessment efficient without sacrificing validity.
316: 
317: ---
318: 
319: ## Part VI — How Onboarding Uses These Modules
320: 
321: The onboarding is NOT a separate system. It is a **composite assessment** that:
322: 
323: 1. **Starts at a middle stage** (Red or Amber) for each line
324: 2. **Runs the stage assessment** for that stage
325: 3. **If passed:** moves UP one stage and tests again
326: 4. **If failed:** moves DOWN one stage and tests again
327: 5. **Converges** when it finds the boundary (passed at S, failed at S+1)
328: 6. **Reports** the highest stage passed with confidence > 0.6
329: 
330: This is a **binary search on stages**, not a staircase on a single parameter. It takes 2-4 stage assessments per line to converge (log₂(8) ≈ 3).
331: 
332: ### 6.1 Onboarding time budget
333: 
334: - 8 lines × 3 stage assessments × 2-3 minutes each = **48-72 minutes total**
335: - This is too long for a single session. Solution: **split across 2-3 sessions**
336: - Session 1: Somatic + Cognitive + Emotional (the "body and mind" session, ~20 min)
337: - Session 2: Moral + Intrapersonal + Spiritual (the "depth" session, ~25 min)
338: - Session 3: Willpower + Interpersonal (the "action" session, ~15 min)
339: 
340: Or: a **quick-calibration mode** that runs only 1 stage assessment per line at the estimated starting point (based on age/self-report), taking ~20 minutes total, with refinement happening during gameplay.
341: 
342: ### 6.2 The onboarding samples from the pool
343: 
344: Each stage assessment module is a **standalone game** that can be:
345: - Used in onboarding (calibration)
346: - Used in combat (as the cognitive task overlay)
347: - Used in practice mode (player chooses to train a specific line/stage)
348: - Used in shadow work (revisiting earlier stages)
349: 
350: This is the key architectural insight: **the same modules serve all four purposes**.
351: 
352: ---
353: 
354: ## Part VII — Implementation Priority
355: 
356: ### Phase 1: Red stage assessments (all 8 lines) — the MVP vertical slice
357: 
358: Since Red is the first gameplay stage, we need all 8 Red-stage assessments first:
359: 1. Cognitive/Red: n=2 n-back + 2-step planning
360: 2. Emotional/Red: self-other emotion split + intensity rating
361: 3. Moral/Red: egocentric dilemmas with LLM-scored justification
362: 4. Intrapersonal/Red: "what are you good at?" + self-concept clarity
363: 5. Spiritual/Red: value-ranking under obvious temptation
364: 6. Somatic/Red: fast RT + rapid alternation
365: 7. Willpower/Red: 3-5s hold under distraction + early-release temptation
366: 8. Interpersonal/Red: predict NPC's simple repeating pattern
367: 
368: ### Phase 2: Amber + Magenta assessments (the adjacent stages)
369: 
370: To calibrate whether someone is below, at, or above Red, we need:
371: - All 8 Magenta assessments (below Red)
372: - All 8 Amber assessments (above Red)
373: 
374: ### Phase 3: Orange + Green assessments
375: 
376: For players who are above Amber.
377: 
378: ### Phase 4: Infrared + Turquoise + White assessments
379: 
380: Edge cases — very low or very high.
381: 
382: ### Phase 5: Composite onboarding
383: 
384: Once all 64 modules exist, build the binary-search onboarding that samples from them.
385: 
386: ---
387: 
388: ## Part VIII — Relationship to Combat
389: 
390: In combat, the cognitive task overlay IS a stage assessment module running in "single-trial" mode:
391: - The encounter scheduler picks a line and stage
392: - The corresponding assessment module provides a single task at that difficulty
393: - The player's response updates their staircase AND contributes to their ongoing assessment
394: - Over many encounters, the system accumulates enough data to refine the altitude with high confidence
395: 
396: This means: **every combat encounter is also an assessment trial**. The game IS the test. The test IS the game.
397: 
398: ---
399: 
400: ## Part IX — File Structure for Implementation
401: 
402: ```
403: src/core/assessments/
404: ├── types.ts                          ← AssessmentTask, ScoringRubric, AssessmentResult, MeasureDimension
405: ├── engine.ts                         ← runAssessment(), scoreTrials(), computeConfidence()
406: ├── cognitive/
407: │   ├── index.ts                      ← exports all 8 stage modules
408: │   ├── infrared.ts                   ← { tasks, rubric, passThreshold }
409: │   ├── magenta.ts
410: │   ├── red.ts
411: │   ├── amber.ts
412: │   ├── orange.ts
413: │   ├── green.ts
414: │   ├── turquoise.ts
415: │   └── white.ts
416: ├── emotional/                        ← same structure
417: ├── moral/                            ← same structure
418: ├── intrapersonal/                    ← same structure
419: ├── spiritual/                        ← same structure
420: ├── somatic/                          ← same structure
421: ├── willpower/                        ← same structure
422: └── interpersonal/                    ← same structure
423: 
424: src/game/assessments/
425: ├── AssessmentScene.ts                ← generic Phaser scene that runs any StageAssessment
426: ├── renderers/
427: │   ├── NBackRenderer.ts             ← renders n-back tasks
428: │   ├── DilemmaRenderer.ts           ← renders moral dilemmas
429: │   ├── ScenarioRenderer.ts          ← renders intrapersonal/spiritual scenarios
430: │   ├── ReactionTimeRenderer.ts      ← renders somatic tasks
431: │   ├── HoldRenderer.ts              ← renders willpower tasks
432: │   ├── PatternRenderer.ts           ← renders interpersonal tasks
433: │   └── EmotionRenderer.ts           ← renders emotional tasks
434: └── CompositeOnboarding.ts           ← the binary-search orchestrator
435: ```
436: 
437: ---
438: 
439: ## Part X — Success Criteria
440: 
441: The system is complete when:
442: 
443: 1. **Each of the 64 modules** can be run independently and produces a multi-dimensional `AssessmentResult`
444: 2. **The composite onboarding** converges on a per-line altitude within 3-4 assessments per line
445: 3. **Combat encounters** draw from the same modules in single-trial mode
446: 4. **The profile** updates based on accumulated assessment data, not single-trial snapshots
447: 5. **LLM scoring** is used for depth/coherence/integration on qualitative lines (Moral, Intrapersonal, Spiritual)
448: 6. **No single assessment can be spoofed** — multiple dimensions cross-validate each other
449: 7. **The player never sees the same content twice** in a single session (large item pools per module)
450: 8. **Confidence is tracked** — the system knows when it's uncertain and schedules more assessment
451: 
452: ---
453: 
454: ## Part XI — Shadow Diagnostics Within Assessment Modules
455: 
456: > Full shadow theory is in `foundations/10-shadow-and-pathology.md`. This section specifies how the 64 assessment modules implement shadow detection.
457: 
458: ### 11.1 Dual-mode operation
459: 
460: Every assessment module operates in two modes:
461: 
462: | Mode | Scoring focus | When triggered |
463: |---|---|---|
464: | **Capacity mode** | Can the player perform at this stage? (accuracy, speed, depth) | Onboarding, advancement testing, combat |
465: | **Shadow mode** | Does the player have a healthy *relationship* to this capacity? (drive-health) | Holonic return encounters, shadow encounters |
466: 
467: The same tasks are used in both modes — only the scoring rubric changes.
468: 
469: ### 11.2 Drive-health probes embedded in every module
470: 
471: Each of the 64 modules includes 4 drive-health probes alongside its capacity tasks:
472: 
473: ```ts
474: export interface StageAssessment {
475:   // ... existing fields from Part II ...
476:   readonly driveProbes: {
477:     readonly agency: DriveProbe;      // "Can you do this independently?"
478:     readonly communion: DriveProbe;   // "Can you share/teach this?"
479:     readonly eros: DriveProbe;        // "Can you let go and try harder?"
480:     readonly agape: DriveProbe;       // "Can you return to easier without shame?"
481:   };
482: }
483: 
484: export interface DriveProbe {
485:   readonly description: string;
486:   readonly task: AssessmentTask;
487:   readonly healthyResponse: string;
488:   readonly addictionSignal: string;   // what addiction looks like here
489:   readonly allergySignal: string;     // what allergy looks like here
490: }
491: ```
492: 
493: ### 11.3 Per-line drive-probe examples
494: 
495: | Line | Stage | Agency probe | Communion probe | Eros probe | Agape probe |
496: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
497: | Cognitive | Red | n=2 without hints | Explain your strategy to NPC | Try n=3 (risk failure) | Do n=1 again fully (not dismissively) |
498: | Emotional | Amber | Identify emotion without group consensus | Help NPC identify their emotion | Attempt complex/mixed emotion | Return to basic emotion naming with care |
499: | Moral | Orange | Make principled choice alone (no social cues) | Justify your choice to someone who disagrees | Consider a dilemma with no clear principle | Revisit a simple fairness scenario with full engagement |
500: | Willpower | Red | Hold without encouragement | Hold while supporting NPC's hold | Attempt longer hold (risk failure) | Do a short easy hold with full presence |
501: 
502: ### 11.4 Shadow scoring output
503: 
504: After running in shadow mode, the module produces:
505: 
506: ```ts
507: export interface ShadowAssessmentResult extends AssessmentResult {
508:   readonly driveHealth: {
509:     readonly agency:    { dark: number; golden: number };  // 0-1 each domain
510:     readonly communion: { dark: number; golden: number };
511:     readonly eros:      { dark: number; golden: number };
512:     readonly agape:     { dark: number; golden: number };
513:   };
514:   readonly darkShadowSeverity: number;    // max pathology across drives in submergent domain
515:   readonly goldenShadowSeverity: number;  // max pathology across drives in emergent domain
516:   readonly dominantPathology: {
517:     drive: Drive;
518:     domain: 'dark' | 'golden';
519:     type: 'addiction' | 'allergy';
520:   } | null;
521: }
522: ```
523: 
524: ---
525: 
526: ## Part XII — Holonic Return: Always Coming Back
527: 
528: ### 12.1 The principle
529: 
530: A player at Orange with an unresolved Red-stage shadow cannot fully function at Orange. The game must always bring the player back to earlier stages where shadows exist. Advancement is not escape — it is deeper integration.
531: 
532: ### 12.2 The return schedule
533: 
534: ```
535: After every 3 encounters at the player's current stage:
536:   1. Scan all earlier stages for shadows with severity > 0.3
537:   2. If found: surface a "return encounter" at that (line, stage)
538:   3. Run the assessment module in SHADOW MODE
539:   4. Score drive-health, not capacity
540:   5. If drive-health exceeds threshold → shadow resolved → integration bonus
541:   6. If not → severity increases by 0.05 (shadow grows if ignored)
542: ```
543: 
544: ### 12.3 The return encounter experience
545: 
546: The player experiences a return encounter as:
547: 1. **Narrative framing:** "Something from your past calls to you..." (not "you failed")
548: 2. **Familiar tasks:** The same mechanics they've seen before, at an easier difficulty
549: 3. **Different scoring:** The game watches HOW they engage, not WHETHER they succeed
550: 4. **Resolution feedback:** "You've integrated this. It's part of you now, not a prison."
551: 
552: ### 12.4 Advancement blocking (refined)
553: 
554: ```
555: To advance from stage S to stage S+1:
556:   - All shadows at stages ≤ S must have severity < 0.3
557:   - OR: player must have attempted resolution (engagement counts)
558:   - Unresolved shadows manifest as debuffs in advancement encounters
559:   - The game NEVER permanently blocks — but makes advancement honestly harder
560: ```
561: 
562: ---
563: 
564: ## Part XIII — The Complete Module Contract
565: 
566: > **Full specifications:**
567: > - Game modalities and multi-game architecture: `foundations/11-game-modalities.md`
568: > - Per-module drive assessment mechanics: `foundations/12-drive-assessment-mechanics.md`
569: > - Shadow/pathology model: `foundations/10-shadow-and-pathology.md`
570: 
571: Each of the 64 assessment modules is a **game pool** (not a single game). Per `foundations/11`, each module must contain ≥ 5 games across ≥ 3 modalities, plus 4 dedicated drive-probe games. The complete contract:
572: 
573: ```ts
574: export interface CompleteStageModule {
575:   // Identity
576:   readonly line: Line;
577:   readonly stage: Stage;
578: 
579:   // Game pool (foundations/11)
580:   readonly games: readonly GameDefinition[];       // ≥ 5 games, ≥ 3 modalities
581:   readonly minimumModalities: 3;
582: 
583:   // Capacity assessment (Part II of this doc)
584:   readonly capacityScoringRubric: ScoringRubric;
585:   readonly minimumTrials: number;
586:   readonly estimatedDurationMs: number;
587: 
588:   // Drive-health probes (foundations/12)
589:   readonly driveProbes: {
590:     agency: DriveProbe;       // task with optional help
591:     communion: DriveProbe;    // cooperative variant
592:     eros: DriveProbe;         // harder-level offer
593:     agape: DriveProbe;        // return-to-easier offer
594:   };
595:   readonly shadowScoringRubric: ScoringRubric;
596: 
597:   // Content pool (anti-repetition)
598:   readonly itemPool: readonly AssessmentItem[];  // ≥ 20 items per game
599:   readonly itemSelector: (used: string[]) => AssessmentItem;
600: 
601:   // LLM rubrics (for qualitative lines)
602:   readonly llmCapacityRubric?: string;
603:   readonly llmDriveHealthRubric?: string;
604: 
605:   // Shadow archetypes (foundations/10)
606:   readonly addictionArchetype: string;   // "The Compulsive Planner"
607:   readonly allergyArchetype: string;     // "The Impulsive Actor"
608:   readonly healthyArchetype: string;     // "The Fluid Thinker"
609: }
610: ```
611: 
612: ### 13.1 Implementation priority (updated)
613: 
614: | Phase | Modules | What's built |
615: |---|---|---|
616: | **Phase 1** | Red × all 8 lines (8 modules) | Capacity tasks + drive probes + shadow archetypes |
617: | **Phase 2** | Amber + Magenta × all 8 lines (16 modules) | Adjacent stages for calibration |
618: | **Phase 3** | Orange + Green × all 8 lines (16 modules) | Mid-range stages |
619: | **Phase 4** | Infrared + Turquoise + White × all 8 lines (24 modules) | Edge stages |
620: | **Phase 5** | Composite onboarding + holonic return system | The orchestration layer |
621: 
622: Each phase delivers **playable, testable modules** that work in isolation before being composed.
623: 
624: ---
625: 
626: ## Part XIV — How This Replaces "Combat-Only" Progression
627: 
628: ### 14.1 The old model (combat-centric)
629: 
630: ```
631: Player → Combat encounter → Win/Lose → XP → Level up
632: ```
633: 
634: This is a single-axis progression that measures nothing developmental.
635: 
636: ### 14.2 The new model (integrative)
637: 
638: ```
639: Player → Assessment encounter (capacity OR shadow mode)
640:   → Multi-dimensional scoring (accuracy, speed, depth, drive-health)
641:     → Profile update (altitude, ray, shadow, drive)
642:       → Encounter scheduler (what to surface next: advancement, shadow, variety)
643:         → Next encounter (tailored to the player's developmental edge)
644: ```
645: 
646: Every encounter is:
647: - A **game** (fun, engaging, has stakes)
648: - An **assessment** (measures something real about the player)
649: - A **developmental catalyst** (pushes the player's edge, surfaces shadows, rewards integration)
650: 
651: ### 14.3 The encounter types
652: 
653: | Type | Purpose | Frequency | Module mode |
654: |---|---|---|---|
655: | **Advancement** | Test capacity at current stage boundary | ~40% of encounters | Capacity mode |
656: | **Shadow return** | Heal earlier-stage shadows | ~20% of encounters | Shadow mode |
657: | **Variety** | Exercise under-used lines | ~20% of encounters | Capacity mode |
658: | **Integration** | Multi-line tasks that require coordination | ~10% of encounters | Both modes |
659: | **Boss synthesis** | Stage-gate exam requiring all lines + drives | ~10% of encounters | Both modes |
660: 
661: This replaces the "battle → XP → level" loop with a **developmental loop** where every encounter serves the player's actual growth.

(End of file - total 661 lines)

### 2.2 Each module exports a `StageAssessment`

```ts
export interface StageAssessment {
  readonly line: Line;
  readonly stage: Stage;
  readonly tasks: readonly AssessmentTask[];
  readonly scoringRubric: ScoringRubric;
  readonly minimumTrials: number;
  readonly estimatedDurationMs: number;
}

export interface AssessmentTask {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly type: TaskType;
  readonly description: string;
  readonly parameters: Record<string, unknown>;
  readonly measures: readonly MeasureDimension[];
}

export type MeasureDimension =
  | 'accuracy'
  | 'response_time'
  | 'consistency'
  | 'depth'
  | 'self_correction'
  | 'complexity_handled'
  | 'transfer'
  | 'metacognition'
  | 'coherence'
  | 'integration';

export interface ScoringRubric {
  /** Minimum score (0-1) to be considered AT this stage */
  readonly passThreshold: number;
  /** How to weight each dimension */
  readonly dimensionWeights: Partial<Record<MeasureDimension, number>>;
  /** LLM rubric prompt for complex scoring (moral, intrapersonal, spiritual) */
  readonly llmRubric?: string;
}

export interface AssessmentResult {
  readonly line: Line;
  readonly stage: Stage;
  readonly passed: boolean;
  readonly confidence: number;  // 0-1, how confident we are in this result
  readonly dimensions: Record<MeasureDimension, number>;
  readonly rawTrials: readonly TrialResult[];
}
```

### 2.3 What each module does

Each stage assessment module defines:
1. **What tasks to run** — specific to that stage's qualitative structure
2. **What to measure** — multiple dimensions, not just accuracy
3. **How to score** — a rubric that combines dimensions into a pass/fail + confidence
4. **What "passing" means** — the qualitative criteria for being AT this stage

## Part IV — Multi-Parameter Scoring

### 4.1 Every assessment measures multiple dimensions

No assessment module produces a single number. Each produces a `Record<MeasureDimension, number>`:

| Dimension | What it measures | How |
|---|---|---|
| `accuracy` | Did they get it right? | % correct |
| `response_time` | How fast? (where speed matters) | Median RT, normalised |
| `consistency` | Same performance across trials? | Variance of accuracy/RT across trials |
| `depth` | How complex/nuanced was their response? | LLM scoring against rubric |
| `self_correction` | Did they catch and fix errors? | % of errors followed by correction |
| `complexity_handled` | What level of complexity could they manage? | Max difficulty level passed |
| `transfer` | Can they apply it in a new context? | Performance on novel variants |
| `metacognition` | Do they know what they know/don't know? | Prediction accuracy (predict own score) |
| `coherence` | Is their response internally consistent? | Cross-trial consistency of reasoning |
| `integration` | Can they hold multiple perspectives/dimensions? | Multi-factor response quality (LLM) |

### 4.2 Dimension weights vary by line and stage

- **Cognitive:** accuracy (0.3), response_time (0.2), complexity_handled (0.3), self_correction (0.2)
- **Emotional:** accuracy (0.2), depth (0.3), consistency (0.2), integration (0.3)
- **Moral:** depth (0.4), coherence (0.3), integration (0.3) — accuracy is meaningless (no "right answer")
- **Intrapersonal:** depth (0.3), metacognition (0.3), coherence (0.2), self_correction (0.2)
- **Spiritual:** coherence (0.4), depth (0.3), consistency (0.3) — under temptation
- **Somatic:** accuracy (0.3), response_time (0.3), consistency (0.4)
- **Willpower:** consistency (0.3), complexity_handled (0.3), transfer (0.2), response_time (0.2)
- **Interpersonal:** accuracy (0.3), response_time (0.2), transfer (0.2), depth (0.3)

### 4.3 LLM scoring for depth/coherence/integration

For lines where the response is qualitative (Moral, Intrapersonal, Spiritual, and higher stages of all lines), the LLM evaluates against a rubric:

```ts
interface LLMScoringRequest {
  readonly playerResponse: string;
  readonly rubric: string;
  readonly stage: Stage;
  readonly line: Line;
  readonly dimensions: MeasureDimension[];
}
```

The rubric is specific to the stage and line. Example for Moral/Green:

> "Score this response on a 0-1 scale for each dimension:
> - depth: Does the response acknowledge multiple valid perspectives without collapsing into relativism?
> - coherence: Is the reasoning internally consistent?
> - integration: Does it hold tension between competing goods without premature resolution?
> A Green-stage moral response recognises that all perspectives have partial truth, while still being able to act. It does not say 'anything goes' (that's regression to Red), nor does it impose a single principle (that's Orange)."

## Part V — The Assessment Engine

### 5.1 How a stage assessment runs

```
1. Load the StageAssessment module for (line, stage)
2. For each task in the module:
   a. Present the task to the player
   b. Collect their response (tap, choice, text, timing)
   c. Score the response on all relevant dimensions
   d. If LLM scoring needed: call evaluateResponse() with the rubric
3. Aggregate dimension scores across all tasks
4. Apply dimension weights from the scoring rubric
5. Compare weighted score to passThreshold
6. Return AssessmentResult { passed, confidence, dimensions }
```

### 5.2 Confidence calculation

Confidence is based on:
- **Number of trials:** more trials = higher confidence
- **Consistency:** low variance across trials = higher confidence
- **Discrimination:** clear pass or clear fail = higher confidence; borderline = lower

```ts
function computeConfidence(results: TrialResult[], passThreshold: number): number {
  const score = weightedScore(results);
  const distance = Math.abs(score - passThreshold);
  const consistency = 1 - variance(results.map(r => r.score));
  const trialFactor = Math.min(1, results.length / 6);
  return distance * consistency * trialFactor;
}
```

### 5.3 Adaptive termination

Each module has a `minimumTrials` (usually 3-4) but can terminate early if:
- Confidence > 0.8 (clear pass or fail)
- All dimensions are clearly above or below threshold

This keeps the assessment efficient without sacrificing validity.

## Part VI — How Onboarding Uses These Modules

The onboarding is NOT a separate system. It is a **composite assessment** that:

1. **Starts at a middle stage** (Red or Amber) for each line
2. **Runs the stage assessment** for that stage
3. **If passed:** moves UP one stage and tests again
4. **If failed:** moves DOWN one stage and tests again
5. **Converges** when it finds the boundary (passed at S, failed at S+1)
6. **Reports** the highest stage passed with confidence > 0.6

This is a **binary search on stages**, not a staircase on a single parameter. It takes 2-4 stage assessments per line to converge (log₂(8) ≈ 3).

### 6.1 Onboarding time budget

- 8 lines × 3 stage assessments × 2-3 minutes each = **48-72 minutes total**
- This is too long for a single session. Solution: **split across 2-3 sessions**
- Session 1: Somatic + Cognitive + Emotional (the "body and mind" session, ~20 min)
- Session 2: Moral + Intrapersonal + Spiritual (the "depth" session, ~25 min)
- Session 3: Willpower + Interpersonal (the "action" session, ~15 min)

Or: a **quick-calibration mode** that runs only 1 stage assessment per line at the estimated starting point (based on age/self-report), taking ~20 minutes total, with refinement happening during gameplay.

### 6.2 The onboarding samples from the pool

Each stage assessment module is a **standalone game** that can be:
- Used in onboarding (calibration)
- Used in combat (as the cognitive task overlay)
- Used in practice mode (player chooses to train a specific line/stage)
- Used in shadow work (revisiting earlier stages)

This is the key architectural insight: **the same modules serve all four purposes**.

## Part VIII — Relationship to Combat

In combat, the cognitive task overlay IS a stage assessment module running in "single-trial" mode:
- The encounter scheduler picks a line and stage
- The corresponding assessment module provides a single task at that difficulty
- The player's response updates their staircase AND contributes to their ongoing assessment
- Over many encounters, the system accumulates enough data to refine the altitude with high confidence

This means: **every combat encounter is also an assessment trial**. The game IS the test. The test IS the game.

## Part X — Success Criteria

The system is complete when:

1. **Each of the 64 modules** can be run independently and produces a multi-dimensional `AssessmentResult`
2. **The composite onboarding** converges on a per-line altitude within 3-4 assessments per line
3. **Combat encounters** draw from the same modules in single-trial mode
4. **The profile** updates based on accumulated assessment data, not single-trial snapshots
5. **LLM scoring** is used for depth/coherence/integration on qualitative lines (Moral, Intrapersonal, Spiritual)
6. **No single assessment can be spoofed** — multiple dimensions cross-validate each other
7. **The player never sees the same content twice** in a single session (large item pools per module)
8. **Confidence is tracked** — the system knows when it's uncertain and schedules more assessment

## Part XI — Shadow Diagnostics Within Assessment Modules

> Full shadow theory is in `foundations/10-shadow-and-pathology.md`. This section specifies how the 64 assessment modules implement shadow detection.

### 11.1 Dual-mode operation

Every assessment module operates in two modes:

| Mode | Scoring focus | When triggered |
|---|---|---|
| **Capacity mode** | Can the player perform at this stage? (accuracy, speed, depth) | Onboarding, advancement testing, combat |
| **Shadow mode** | Does the player have a healthy *relationship* to this capacity? (drive-health) | Holonic return encounters, shadow encounters |

The same tasks are used in both modes — only the scoring rubric changes.

### 11.2 Drive-health probes embedded in every module

Each of the 64 modules includes 4 drive-health probes alongside its capacity tasks:

```ts

    readonly communion: DriveProbe;   // "Can you share/teach this?"
    readonly eros: DriveProbe;        // "Can you let go and try harder?"
    readonly agape: DriveProbe;       // "Can you return to easier without shame?"
  };
}

export interface DriveProbe {
  readonly description: string;
  readonly task: AssessmentTask;
  readonly healthyResponse: string;
  readonly addictionSignal: string;   // what addiction looks like here

### 11.3 Per-line drive-probe examples

| Line | Stage | Agency probe | Communion probe | Eros probe | Agape probe |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cognitive | Red | n=2 without hints | Explain your strategy to NPC | Try n=3 (risk failure) | Do n=1 again fully (not dismissively) |
| Emotional | Amber | Identify emotion without group consensus | Help NPC identify their emotion | Attempt complex/mixed emotion | Return to basic emotion naming with care |
| Moral | Orange | Make principled choice alone (no social cues) | Justify your choice to someone who disagrees | Consider a dilemma with no clear principle | Revisit a simple fairness scenario with full engagement |
| Willpower | Red | Hold without encouragement | Hold while supporting NPC's hold | Attempt longer hold (risk failure) | Do a short easy hold with full presence |

## Part XII — Holonic Return: Always Coming Back

### 12.1 The principle

A player at Orange with an unresolved Red-stage shadow cannot fully function at Orange. The game must always bring the player back to earlier stages where shadows exist. Advancement is not escape — it is deeper integration.

### 12.2 The return schedule

```
After every 3 encounters at the player's current stage:
  1. Scan all earlier stages for shadows with severity > 0.3
  2. If found: surface a "return encounter" at that (line, stage)
  3. Run the assessment module in SHADOW MODE
  4. Score drive-health, not capacity
  5. If drive-health exceeds threshold → shadow resolved → integration bonus
  6. If not → severity increases by 0.05 (shadow grows if ignored)
```

### 12.3 The return encounter experience

The player experiences a return encounter as:
1. **Narrative framing:** "Something from your past calls to you..." (not "you failed")
2. **Familiar tasks:** The same mechanics they've seen before, at an easier difficulty
3. **Different scoring:** The game watches HOW they engage, not WHETHER they succeed
4. **Resolution feedback:** "You've integrated this. It's part of you now, not a prison."

### 12.4 Advancement blocking (refined)

```
To advance from stage S to stage S+1:
  - All shadows at stages ≤ S must have severity < 0.3
  - OR: player must have attempted resolution (engagement counts)
  - Unresolved shadows manifest as debuffs in advancement encounters
  - The game NEVER permanently blocks — but makes advancement honestly harder
```

  readonly line: Line;
  readonly stage: Stage;

  // Game pool (foundations/11)
  readonly games: readonly GameDefinition[];       // ≥ 5 games, ≥ 3 modalities
  readonly minimumModalities: 3;

  // Capacity assessment (Part II of this doc)
  readonly capacityScoringRubric: ScoringRubric;
  readonly minimumTrials: number;
  readonly estimatedDurationMs: number;

  // Drive-health probes (foundations/12)
  readonly driveProbes: {
    agency: DriveProbe;       // task with optional help
    communion: DriveProbe;    // cooperative variant
    eros: DriveProbe;         // harder-level offer
    agape: DriveProbe;        // return-to-easier offer
  };
  readonly shadowScoringRubric: ScoringRubric;

  // Content pool (anti-repetition)
  readonly itemPool: readonly AssessmentItem[];  // ≥ 20 items per game
  readonly itemSelector: (used: string[]) => AssessmentItem;

  // LLM rubrics (for qualitative lines)
  readonly llmCapacityRubric?: string;
  readonly llmDriveHealthRubric?: string;

  // Shadow archetypes (foundations/10)
  readonly addictionArchetype: string;   // "The Compulsive Planner"
  readonly allergyArchetype: string;     // "The Impulsive Actor"
  readonly healthyArchetype: string;     // "The Fluid Thinker"
}
```

### 13.1 Implementation priority (updated)

| Phase | Modules | What's built |
|---|---|---|
| **Phase 1** | Red × all 8 lines (8 modules) | Capacity tasks + drive probes + shadow archetypes |
| **Phase 2** | Amber + Magenta × all 8 lines (16 modules) | Adjacent stages for calibration |
| **Phase 3** | Orange + Green × all 8 lines (16 modules) | Mid-range stages |
| **Phase 4** | Infrared + Turquoise + White × all 8 lines (24 modules) | Edge stages |
| **Phase 5** | Composite onboarding + holonic return system | The orchestration layer |

Each phase delivers **playable, testable modules** that work in isolation before being composed.

---

## Part XIV — How This Replaces "Combat-Only" Progression

### 14.1 The old model (combat-centric)

```
Player → Combat encounter → Win/Lose → XP → Level up
```

This is a single-axis progression that measures nothing developmental.

### 14.2 The new model (integrative)

```
Player → Assessment encounter (capacity OR shadow mode)
  → Multi-dimensional scoring (accuracy, speed, depth, drive-health)
    → Profile update (altitude, ray, shadow, drive)
      → Encounter scheduler (what to surface next: advancement, shadow, variety)
        → Next encounter (tailored to the player's developmental edge)
```

Every encounter is:
- A **game** (fun, engaging, has stakes)
- An **assessment** (measures something real about the player)
- A **developmental catalyst** (pushes the player's edge, surfaces shadows, rewards integration)

### 14.3 The encounter types

| Type | Purpose | Frequency | Module mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Advancement** | Test capacity at current stage boundary | ~40% of encounters | Capacity mode |
| **Shadow return** | Heal earlier-stage shadows | ~20% of encounters | Shadow mode |
| **Variety** | Exercise under-used lines | ~20% of encounters | Capacity mode |
| **Integration** | Multi-line tasks that require coordination | ~10% of encounters | Both modes |
| **Boss synthesis** | Stage-gate exam requiring all lines + drives | ~10% of encounters | Both modes |

This replaces the "battle → XP → level" loop with a **developmental loop** where every encounter serves the player's actual growth.
